title: The first installation
hook: the day the Adi Granth was first placed in the Harmandir in 1604 is celebrated in late summer

segments.voice: Yesterday, Guru Har Krishan's gurpurab, and your line: the child healer. Did you do one small thing for someone unwell? We've walked through the Gurus' days. Now, two days for the book itself. Day six hundred ninety.

A passport. A house deed. A letter from someone who's gone. Nobody tosses papers like that into a bag; they get carried with two hands. In 1604, Sikhs carried a book that way: the words of the Gurus and saints, gathered over years and copied by hand, brought for the first time into the building raised to house it. Who carried it? Where did it sit? And where did the Guru sit? Today: the first installation.
screen: `HELD WITH TWO HANDS.` → `A BOOK COPIED BY HAND.` → `CARRIED IN FOR THE FIRST TIME.`

segments.voice: By the early 1600s, Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, had gathered the hymns of the first five Gurus, along with those of Hindu and Muslim saints whose words shared the Gurus' vision. Bhai Gurdas wrote them out as scribe. The finished volume was called the Adi Granth, the first book. In 1604, it was carried into the newly built Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar and opened there for the first time. Sikh tradition remembers the scene. Baba Buddha, a revered elder who had known Guru Nanak himself, carried the Granth on his head. He was appointed its first granthi, the one who reads it and cares for it. The Granth was placed on a raised seat, and Guru Arjan sat below it. The Guru, at a lower level than the book. That small detail says a great deal about what was coming. Then the Granth was opened at random, as it still is each day, for the first hukamnama, the day's command. Tradition gives the first one as a shabad of Guru Arjan in Raag Suhi, on Ang seven eighty-three. In paraphrase: the Lord Himself stood up to complete the work of His saints; the Lord came to do the work. Sikhs mark this day as the Pehla Prakash, the first opening, in late summer. At the Harmandir Sahib it's celebrated with kirtan, lights and a great procession. And every morning since, in that same building, the Granth has been carried in and opened again: the word, installed.
screen: `GURU ARJAN GATHERS THE ADI GRANTH.` · `BABA BUDDHA CARRIES IT IN.` · `THE GURU SITS BELOW THE BOOK.` · `THE FIRST HUKAMNAMA.` · then, large: `THE WORD INSTALLED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: open a book reverently. Take any book that matters to you: a scripture, a gutka, a book of poems, a book someone gave you. Hold it with both hands. Before you open it, pause. Then open it slowly, wherever it falls, and read just one line, as if it were addressed to you today. Sit with that line until the bell. If you pray, you can say Waheguru before you open it. The bell holds the time.
The first installation. The day in 1604 the Adi Granth was first opened in the Harmandir Sahib, carried in by Baba Buddha, with Guru Arjan seated below it.
Your line: the word installed. Today, give one book or one set of words a place of honor where you live, even a small one. Day six hundred ninety.

howItsDone: Sikhs celebrate the Pehla Prakash, the first installation of the Adi Granth in the Harmandir Sahib in 1604, with kirtan, illuminations and a procession at Amritsar, and with special programs in gurdwaras.

fork.setup: it's 1604, and the Adi Granth has been carried into the Harmandir Sahib. where does Guru Arjan sit?
options: on a throne above the Granth.
beside Baba Buddha at the door.
fork.reveal: the Guru sat lower than the book, a detail Sikhs see as pointing to the Granth's future as Guru.

original.note: Punjabi: light, opening; the Pehla Prakash is the Granth's first opening in 1604.

trapdoor: what you thought: the installation was putting a book on a shelf.
what it means: the Word was given the place of honor, above even the living Guru.
what a scholar hears: the Kartarpur manuscript associated with Bhai Gurdas is often identified with the 1604 volume; the first hukamnama (Suhi M5, Ang 783) is given by tradition.
